answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit work; a randomly selected task then triggers a challenge, and the agent forfeits that stake if it cannot provide a verifiable result within the deadline. Splitting into many identities does not multiply influence for free: every identity needs its own locked capital, while honest agents recover theirs. The cost to a sybil attacker is capital tied up across identities, plus losses on failed challenges, whether operating at zenith, across an ocean, or in karst territory.
